chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said:

I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) dealt with the people of the Qiblah (Muslims) in a manner contrary to the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the people of polytheism.' He said, 'He became angry, then sat down, then said: By Allah, he dealt with them with the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Conquest.'

Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) wrote to Malik, while he was at the forefront of his vanguard on the Day of Basra, instructing: 'Do not thrust (the spear) into one who is not facing you, do not kill a fleeing one, do not continue striking an injured one, and whoever closes his door, he is safe.'

So he took the letter and placed it in front of him upon the saddle before reading it, then said, 'Fight.' So they fought them until they made them enter the markets of Basra. Then he opened the letter, read it, then ordered a caller who called out with what was in the letter.

key_terms.سِيرَةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Conduct/Practice of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What were the specific orders Imam Ali gave to Malik al-Ashtar during the Battle of Basra?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the strategic wisdom of Malik al-Ashtar during the Battle of Basra, illustrating the Shia scholarly view that his delay in reading Imam Ali’s (AS) letter was a calculated military decision to ensure victory before announcing terms of surrender, rather than an act of disobedience. The narrative reinforces the principle of 'Amn al-Dhimmah' (guarantee of safety) for those who close their doors, a key concept in Islamic jurisprudence regarding war booty and prisoners. It also connects to the broader theme of Imam Ali’s consistent adherence to the Prophet’s (PBUH) conduct, as affirmed by Imam al-Sajjad (AS) in the opening dialogue.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban Bin usman, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,

‘I said to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup> dealt among the people of the Qiblah (Muslims) with opposite to the way of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> among the people of the Polytheism’. So he<sup>asws</sup> got angered, then said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> dealt among them with the way of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> on the day of the victory.

Ali<sup>asws</sup> wrote to Maalik, and he was at the forefront on the day of Al-Basra, that he would not thrust among the ones who are not facing him, nor would he kill a fleeing one, nor would he attack upon the injured, and the one who locks his door, so he is safe.

So he (Maalik) took the letter and placed it in front of him upon the saddle before reading it, then said, ‘Fight’. So they fought them until they made them enter the markets of Al-Basra. Then he opened the letter, so he read it, then ordered a caller, so he called out with was was in the letter’.
en.sarwar: 3. AI-Husayn ibn Muhammad af-‘Ash’ariy has narrated from Mu’alfa’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy who has said the following:

“I once said to Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘The way Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, dealt with people of Qiblah was different from the way the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, dealt with the pagans.’ He the narrator has said, ‘He (the Imam) became angry and sat in his place;’ then said, ‘He by Allah, did deal with them according to the method of the Messenger of Allah on the day of victory.

On the day of al- Basra, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote to Malik who was on the front line, and commanded him, “You must not hit anyone except advancing attackers, you must not kill the fleeing, you must not hurt the wounded and those who close their doors have immunity.”

Malik received the letter of commandment but he placed it in front of himself on the saddle before reading. He then ordered them to fight and they fought until they were pushed into the alleys of al-Basra. He then opened the letter of commandment and ordered to announce the contents of the letter of commandment.’”
